newsitem.title: FRANCE: Firebomb hits Jewish school near Lyon, no one hurt.
newsitem.headline: Firebomb hits Jewish school near Lyon, no one hurt.

text.p: A petrol bomb exploded overnight outside a Jewish building in a suburb of the French city of Lyon, near where a car bomb injured 14 people at a Jewish school in 1995, police said on Friday.
Local Jewish leader Alain Jackubowicz said the petrol bomb, which was thrown in the middle of the night, caused no damage when it exploded outside the Villeurbanne centre for Jewish studies.
A second unexploded firebomb was found outside a synagogue in Lyon itself and removed by police. No one claimed responsibility for either incident.
In September 1995, a car bomb exploded outside another Jewish school in Villeurbanne amid a wave of bombings in France claimed by Algerian Islamic extremists.
The car bomb, which exploded minutes before schoolchildren were due to leave for the day, injured 14 people and caused major damage. A school clock running late helped avoid a heavier toll.

In March, a crude bomb exploded at a Paris mosque run by a liberal Moslem cleric, slightly injuring a caretaker. In December, the editor of a weekly Jewish newspaper received a letter bomb which failed to explode.
